meta.title: Fieldnotes — Series A pitch, November 2026
meta.description: Series A pitch for Fieldnotes, a tabbed team notebook: wiki problem, product, why now, traction, market, competition, model, team and a $14M ask.

slides.heading: Team notes that stay findable, with no wiki to maintain.
slides.lead: Raising $14M to take the tabbed notebook to teams.
slides.notes: Say the sentence, then stop. Mara presents; Jonas takes product questions.

slides.heading: Teams lose five hours a week hunting for their own notes
slides.body: Wikis die within a quarter. Notes scatter across docs and chats. Source: 2026 survey, 1,840 workers.
slides.aside: 5.2 hours a week, per person, spent searching.

slides.heading: Fieldnotes files every page under a tab you already remember
slides.lead: Write first. Tab later. Find it in two taps.

slides.heading: Three shifts since 2023 turned a personal notebook into a team tool
Weekly writers grew from 21k to 92k in five quarters
slides.lead: Source: Fieldnotes product analytics, weekly actives at quarter end.
slides.notes: No paid acquisition. 74% of sign-ups come from a shared page.

slides.heading: Six in ten writers still use Fieldnotes a year later
Three design choices make a notebook work for a whole team
The business
slides.lead: Who pays, how many of them, and why we win.

slides.heading: 4.1 million small teams make a $2.9B yearly market

stats.label: Teams of 5–50 in US and EU

slides.heading: Wikis demand structure up front; Fieldnotes adds it later
slides.left:
Templates first.
One owner keeps it alive.
40 near-matches per search.
slides.right:
Write now, tab later.
Everyone files.
Search knows the tab.
slides.notes: Name the wikis by category, not brand. The point is the order of work.

slides.quote: We tried two wikis in a year. Fieldnotes is the first place my crew actually writes.
slides.by: Priya Raman · Site lead, Halden Civil Engineering

slides.heading: Team seats bring 78% of our $6.4M ARR
The founders have shipped note apps to 30 million people
$14M takes findable team notes from 92k to 400k writers
